basis: Every gate the workflow ran is present in the local runner, asserted by test rather than by inspection.
The loop refused this candidate twice for undeclared paths; the packet document was amended with recorded reasons rather than the check widened.
No secret value enters the repository; .env stays ignored and .env.example is asserted to carry names only.
what_this_trades_away: Independent execution. A hosted runner validated on a machine the author did not control; a local run does not. That independence was already notional here — the workflow never once scheduled a job — but removing it makes the absence permanent rather than temporary.

The second copy of the gate list. The parity test used to catch a dropped gate by disagreeing with the workflow; now it asserts the required set directly, which is weaker in that it can be edited in the same commit as the script.
residual_risk: Validation now depends on a person remembering to run it. That is the honest cost of the decision and is stated in AGENTS.md rather than left implicit.
A contributor without the repository checked out cannot validate a change at all.
Default model ids are unset in .env.example except the Architect seat; an unset variable fails closed at call time, which is intended but means the first live call will surface several at once.
discovery_candidates: OBS-VAL-001-a-gate-that-cannot-run-is-worse-than-none: the workflow enforced nothing while appearing to, and a red badge everyone learns to ignore is how a real failure gets ignored too. Removing it is not a loss of coverage; it is the removal of a false claim of coverage.

OBS-VAL-001-history-is-not-a-lint-target: three times in this packet the correct move was to leave a completed record naming a thing that no longer exists, rather than edit it to satisfy a check. Evidence says what was true, not what is.
